subject: blueprintSpitfire
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: Spitfire fighter plane.
Style: cyanotype blueprint.
reasoning:
I'm planning a Spitfire model in cyanotype blueprint style—flat blue tones with white outline details—as a single TS module, keeping the geometry simple as a static part-based build without joints since no moving pieces are needed beyond maybe the propeller.

I'm working out real-world dimensions (9.1m length, 11.2m wingspan) and a level ground pose for readability: wheels touching y=0, fuselage axis around 1.9m so the prop tip clears the ground. For the blueprint aesthetic, I'm settling on a deep cyan-blue body with lighter blue panels, white panel lines, rivet rows, and roundels rendered as concentric rings.

Now I'm defining the fuselage as a series of lofted cross-sections from tail to nose, specifying width, height, and vertical offset at each station to shape the taper from the slender tail through the wider cockpit area up toward the nose.

I'm also adding a cone-shaped spinner at the nose tip, oriented along the fuselage axis to cap the front end.

For the propeller, I'm planning three blades arranged radially around the spinner, each a thin rotated box positioned at an angle offset so they form an even circular pattern.

Now I'm sketching the wings as an elliptical planform, extruding an outline with span-wise taper from a 2.5m root chord down to about 0.9m at the tip, using cross products to orient thickness correctly along the extrusion axes.

Still plotting wing outline points...

Adding thin control-surface divider lines for the aileron and flap with simple rods, then stacking flat disc cylinders to form the concentric roundel markings on the wing uppers.

Shrinking the roundel radius down, then shifting to the tail fin: I'm plotting its outline in the z-y plane with a swept, rounded leading edge rising from the fuselage up to a tapered tip.

Positioning the fin base near the fuselage centerline and sketching a thin rudder hinge rod running from near the tail to the fin's upper edge, then moving on to defining the tailplane shape.

Now I'm sketching the elliptical tailplane geometry with a tapered outline and placing it symmetrically behind the fuselage, plus adding the elevator hinge rod. For the canopy, I'm scaling a sphere into a flattened bubble shape with a light cyan glow, adding white frame rods and ring bars, and sketching a tilted windscreen box.

Still working out the canopy frame tori positioning...

Setting torus radius slightly bigger than the canopy, then adding radiator housings under each wing and sketching landing gear legs that splay outward from the wing to the axle.

Now I'm working out wheel placement and track width—settling on legs angled from the wing root down to the wheel hubs, with dark tires and white hub rings.

For the tail wheel, I'm sizing a small strut that reaches down to ground level, but it ends up unrealistically long since the fuselage sits fairly high there. I consider tilting the whole model to mimic the authentic tail-down Spitfire stance, but decide it's simpler to just keep everything level and accept the longer strut.

Now I'm placing six small exhaust stub cylinders along each side of the nose cowling, positioned near the engine section with a slight outward direction to mimic the real stacks.

Turning to armaments, I'm adding two forward wing cannons as thin white rods projecting ahead of the leading edge on each side. Then I'm working on fuselage panel lines, generating closed loop paths around the hull at several stations and sweeping thin tubes along them to create roughly nine rivet-line rings.

Writing fuselage markings...

I'll go with countershade for the fuselage, dark Prussian blue on top and lighter blue belly, and apply the same technique to the wings so top faces read darker than the bottom. I'll skip adding a grid, dimension callouts, or text decals to keep things clean, but I'll add small wing-tip nav lights as a subtle detail.

I'm skipping the cockpit interior and pilot headrest for simplicity, but adding a subtle pale cyan glow to the canopy glass. I'm setting up helper functions for drawing rod-based lines and wrapping the fuselage ring-panel generation in a try/catch since the loop path could miss the plane depending on z-range, and I'm working out the wing rib line heights based on the wing's thickness and vertical offset.

I'm now positioning the wing rib boxes along the span and computing the aileron and flap hinge lines by placing them at a fraction of the chord toward the trailing edge, plus adding a small wingtip light.

For the roundel markings, I'm layering white and dark blue discs with slight vertical offsets to sit flush on the wing's upper surface at the computed chord position, using white spheres for the tip light since the palette is blue-focused.

For the fuselage sides I'll use surface raycasting to find the x position, falling back to .3 if needed. Then I'm placing the prop hub and spinner cone with a white ring line, plus fuselage cowl rings at several z-depths, and positioning the under-wing radiator box relative to the wing bottom.

Adding white radiator inner lines, finalizing the fuselage loft end caps, and placing the spinner backplate cylinder flush against the nose cowl at z=3.2, with a small intake box tucked under the nose — skipping the chin radiator housing and carb intake bump as unnecessary detail.

Now I'm sorting out the fin and tailplane geometry: extruding the vertical fin along its outline with absolute z coordinates, mirroring the tailplane across x with a thickness profile, and checking that the fin's top height clears the propeller tip while the tires sit flush at ground level. I'm also setting up color palette constants and the tire cylinder dimensions oriented along the x-axis.

Still writing landing gear and prop details...
